_about: Curated entries for regions and eras where Wikidata has few dated events: archaeological cultures, early states, first contacts, and Central Asia in every era. Written for GeoHistory from general knowledge. Dates marked "approx" are scholarly estimates and are shown with "c."; an approximate entry counts as verified when Wikidata dates the linked article within 50 years of it, an exact one only when the year matches.
period: Early history of thinly recorded regions (North America, Latin America, Oceania, Southeast Asia, sub-Saharan Africa before 1500) and Central Asia

events.label: Poverty Point earthworks built
events.desc: Hunter-gatherers build concentric earthen ridges and mounds in the lower Mississippi valley.

events.label: Adena culture
events.desc: Mound-building communities of the Ohio valley.

events.label: Hopewell tradition
events.desc: A network of mound-building societies in eastern North America linked by long-distance exchange of copper, shell and obsidian.

events.label: Mississippian culture
events.desc: Maize-farming chiefdoms with towns of platform mounds across the Mississippi valley and the Southeast.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Great houses built in Chaco Canyon
events.desc: Ancestral Puebloans build multi-storey stone great houses and roads in the San Juan Basin.

events.label: Norse settlement of Greenland begins
events.desc: Erik the Red leads settlers from Iceland to south-western Greenland; the settlements last until the 15th century.

events.label: Norse reach Newfoundland
events.desc: Norse voyagers build a short-lived base at the northern tip of Newfoundland; wood cut there has been dated to 1021.

events.label: Thule people spread across the Arctic
events.desc: Ancestors of the Inuit move east from Alaska across Arctic Canada to Greenland.

events.label: Cahokia at its height
events.desc: The largest town north of Mexico, with Monks Mound and perhaps 10,000 to 20,000 people, grows quickly from about 1050.

events.label: Cliff dwellings built at Mesa Verde
events.desc: Ancestral Puebloans build and then leave the cliff dwellings of Mesa Verde.

events.label: Caral–Supe civilization
events.desc: The oldest known cities in the Americas, on the coast of Peru.

events.label: Monte Albán founded
events.desc: The Zapotec capital is built on a levelled hilltop in the Valley of Oaxaca.

events.label: Moche culture
events.desc: A society of the northern Peruvian coast, known for its portrait pottery and adobe pyramids.

events.label: Tiwanaku state
events.desc: A highland state centred near Lake Titicaca.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Wari Empire
events.desc: A highland state in central Peru whose roads and administrative centres foreshadow the Inca.

events.label: Classic Maya collapse
events.desc: The great cities of the southern Maya lowlands are abandoned over a century and a half.

events.label: Toltec ascendancy at Tula
events.desc: Tula is the leading city of central Mexico.

events.label: Kingdom of Chimor
events.desc: The Chimú state of the north coast of Peru, ruled from Chan Chan, is conquered by the Inca about 1470.

events.label: Tenochtitlan founded
events.desc: The Mexica found their city on an island in Lake Texcoco (the traditional date).

events.label: Pachacuti begins the Inca expansion
events.desc: Pachacuti becomes ruler of Cusco and turns a small kingdom into an empire.

events.label: Machu Picchu built
events.desc: An Inca royal estate is built on a ridge above the Urubamba river.

events.label: Lapita culture
events.desc: Seafarers with distinctive stamped pottery settle the islands from the Bismarck Archipelago to Tonga and Samoa; their descendants become the Polynesians.

events.label: Tuʻi Tonga line of kings begins
events.desc: The Tongan paramount chiefs begin to extend their influence over neighbouring islands.

events.label: Megalithic Nan Madol built
events.desc: The stone city of the Saudeleur rulers is built on artificial islets off Pohnpei.

events.label: Moai carved on Easter Island
events.desc: Islanders carve and raise nearly a thousand stone statues.

events.label: Polynesians settle New Zealand
events.desc: Ancestors of the Māori arrive by canoe from eastern Polynesia in the late 13th century.

events.label: Torres sails through Torres Strait
events.desc: A Spanish expedition passes between New Guinea and Australia.

events.label: Abel Tasman reaches Tasmania and New Zealand
events.desc: A Dutch East India Company expedition sights Tasmania in November and New Zealand in December.

events.label: First voyage of James Cook
events.desc: Cook observes the transit of Venus at Tahiti, circles New Zealand and charts the east coast of Australia in 1770.

events.label: Death of James Cook
events.desc: Cook is killed at Kealakekua Bay on the island of Hawaii on 14 February.

events.label: First Fleet lands at Sydney Cove
events.desc: Eleven British ships carrying convicts found the colony of New South Wales on 26 January.

events.label: Mutiny on the Bounty
events.desc: Fletcher Christian and part of the crew seize the ship from William Bligh near Tonga on 28 April.

events.label: Battle of Nuʻuanu
events.desc: Kamehameha I conquers Oahu.

events.label: Australian gold rushes begin
events.desc: Gold finds in New South Wales and Victoria bring a rush of immigrants.

events.label: Women win the vote in New Zealand
events.desc: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country where women can vote in national elections.

events.label: Dong Son culture
events.desc: A Bronze Age culture of the Red River valley, known for its large bronze drums.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Trung sisters' rebellion
events.desc: Two sisters lead a rising against Han Chinese rule in northern Vietnam.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Funan
events.desc: The earliest known state of mainland Southeast Asia, in the Mekong delta, trading with India and China.

events.label: Champa founded
events.desc: Chinese records date the beginning of the Cham kingdom of Lâm Ấp on the coast of central Vietnam.

events.label: Earliest dated Srivijaya inscription
events.desc: An Old Malay inscription near Palembang records a royal expedition; Srivijaya goes on to control the Strait of Malacca.

events.label: Borobudur built
events.desc: The Sailendra dynasty builds the world's largest Buddhist monument in central Java.

events.label: Khmer Empire founded
events.desc: Jayavarman II declares himself universal monarch, the traditional beginning of the Angkor period.

events.label: Prambanan built
events.desc: A large Hindu temple compound is built in central Java.

events.label: Lý dynasty founded
events.desc: Lý Công Uẩn takes the throne of Đại Cồ Việt and moves the capital to Thăng Long (Hanoi) the next year.

events.label: Chola raid on Srivijaya
events.desc: A fleet of the Chola king Rajendra I sacks ports of Srivijaya.

events.label: Anawrahta becomes king of Pagan
events.desc: He unites the Irrawaddy valley and promotes Theravada Buddhism.

events.label: Angkor Wat built
events.desc: Suryavarman II builds the temple in the first half of the 12th century.

events.label: Jayavarman VII becomes king of the Khmer
events.desc: He drives out the Cham, builds Angkor Thom and the Bayon, and makes Buddhism the state religion.

events.label: Sukhothai Kingdom founded
events.desc: A Thai kingdom breaks away from Khmer rule.

events.label: First Mongol invasion of Burma
events.desc: Yuan armies defeat the Pagan Kingdom, which breaks up.

events.label: Battle of Bạch Đằng (1288)
events.desc: Trần Hưng Đạo destroys a Yuan fleet, ending the third Mongol invasion of Đại Việt.

events.label: Mongol invasion of Java
events.desc: A Yuan expedition is drawn into a Javanese civil war and driven out; Raden Wijaya founds Majapahit.

events.label: Ayutthaya founded
events.desc: A new Thai kingdom is founded on the lower Chao Phraya.

events.label: Lan Xang founded
events.desc: Fa Ngum unites the Lao principalities.

events.label: Malacca founded
events.desc: Parameswara founds a port that becomes the main market of Southeast Asia.

events.label: Lê dynasty founded
events.desc: Lê Lợi drives out the Ming occupation and takes the throne of Đại Việt.

events.label: Fall of Angkor
events.desc: An Ayutthayan army takes the Khmer capital, which is later abandoned.

events.label: Đại Việt conquers Vijaya
events.desc: Lê Thánh Tông takes the Cham capital and annexes most of Champa.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Nok culture
events.desc: An early iron-using society of central Nigeria, known for its terracotta sculpture.

events.label: Djenné-Djenno settled
events.desc: One of the oldest known towns in sub-Saharan Africa grows up in the inland Niger delta.

events.label: King Ezana of Aksum adopts Christianity
events.desc: Aksum becomes one of the first states to make Christianity its official religion.

events.label: Ghana Empire
events.desc: The kingdom of Wagadou controls the trade in gold and salt across the western Sahara.

events.label: Igbo-Ukwu bronzes made
events.desc: Elaborate cast bronzes are buried in a shrine and a rich grave in south-eastern Nigeria.

events.label: Kilwa Sultanate founded
events.desc: According to its chronicle, a Persian prince founds the dynasty of the Swahili trading city.

events.label: Kingdom of Mapungubwe
events.desc: A state on the Limpopo trades gold and ivory to the Indian Ocean coast.

events.label: Great Zimbabwe built
events.desc: The stone-walled capital of a Shona kingdom.

events.label: Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela
events.desc: Eleven churches are cut from the living rock under the Zagwe kings.

events.label: Battle of Kirina
events.desc: Sundiata Keita defeats the Sosso king Sumanguru and founds the Mali Empire.

events.label: Solomonic dynasty restored
events.desc: Yekuno Amlak overthrows the Zagwe and founds the dynasty that rules Ethiopia until 1974.

events.label: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
events.desc: The ruler of Mali travels through Cairo with so much gold that its price falls.

events.label: Kingdom of Kongo founded
events.desc: A kingdom forms south of the lower Congo river.

events.label: Ewuare becomes Oba of Benin
events.desc: He rebuilds Benin City and expands the kingdom.

events.label: Portuguese reach Cape Verde, the westernmost point of Africa
events.desc: Dinis Dias sails past the mouth of the Senegal river.

events.label: Sunni Ali becomes ruler of Songhai
events.desc: He takes Timbuktu and Djenné and makes Songhai the leading power on the Niger.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Elmina Castle built
events.desc: The Portuguese build a fortified trading post on the Gold Coast.

events.label: King of Kongo baptised
events.desc: Nzinga a Nkuwu takes the name João I.

events.label: Askia Muhammad takes the Songhai throne
events.desc: Under him the empire reaches its greatest extent.

events.label: Botai culture
events.desc: Hunters and herders of the northern Kazakh steppe, with some of the earliest evidence for the keeping of horses.

events.label: Oxus civilization
events.desc: Bronze Age towns of the oases of present-day Turkmenistan and northern Afghanistan.

events.label: Andronovo culture
events.desc: Bronze Age herders of the steppe from the Urals to the Yenisei.

events.label: Alexandria Eschate founded
events.desc: Alexander the Great founds "Alexandria the Farthest" on the Syr Darya.

events.label: War of the Heavenly Horses
events.desc: A Han Chinese army marches to Fergana to obtain its horses.

events.label: Muslim conquest of Transoxiana
events.desc: Arab armies cross the Oxus; Qutayba ibn Muslim takes Bukhara and Samarkand in the early 8th century.

events.label: Samanid dynasty begins to rule Transoxiana
events.desc: A Persian dynasty governing for the Abbasids makes Bukhara a centre of Persian culture.

events.label: Karakhanids take Bukhara; the Samanid state ends
events.desc: Turkic dynasties now rule Transoxiana.

events.label: Battle of Qatwan
events.desc: The Qara Khitai defeat the Seljuk sultan Sanjar near Samarkand.

events.label: Mongols take Bukhara
events.desc: Genghis Khan's army captures the city.

events.label: Timur takes power
events.desc: Timur makes himself master of Transoxiana with Samarkand as his capital.

events.label: Death of Timur
events.desc: Timur dies at Otrar at the start of a campaign against China.

events.label: Ulugh Beg's observatory built
events.desc: Timur's grandson builds an observatory at Samarkand, where a great star catalogue is compiled.

events.label: Kazakh Khanate founded
events.desc: Janibek and Kerei lead their followers away from the Uzbek khan.

events.label: Uzbeks under Shaybani Khan take Samarkand
events.desc: The Shaybanids end Timurid rule in Transoxiana.

events.label: Khanate of Khiva founded
events.desc: An Uzbek dynasty takes power in Khwarazm.

events.label: Khanate of Kokand founded
events.desc: The Fergana valley breaks away from Bukhara.

events.label: Kazakh Junior Horde accepts Russian protection
events.desc: Abul Khair swears allegiance to the Russian empress.

events.label: Emirate of Bukhara founded
events.desc: The Manghit dynasty takes the throne of Bukhara.

events.label: Russian Turkestan created
events.desc: Two years after taking Tashkent, Russia sets up a governor-generalship there.

events.label: Russia conquers Khiva
events.desc: The khanate becomes a Russian protectorate.

events.label: Russia annexes Kokand
events.desc: The khanate is abolished.

events.label: Panjdeh incident
events.desc: A clash between Russian and Afghan troops brings Russia and Britain close to war.

events.label: Andijan uprising
events.desc: A rising against Russian rule in the Fergana valley is put down.

events.label: Soviet Central Asia divided into national republics
events.wiki: National delimitation in the Soviet Union
events.desc: The Uzbek and Turkmen republics are created; the others follow by 1936.

events.label: Kazakh famine
events.desc: Forced collectivisation and settlement of the nomads kill well over a million Kazakhs.

events.label: Ashgabat earthquake
events.desc: The Turkmen capital is destroyed on 6 October.

events.label: Virgin Lands campaign
events.desc: The Soviet Union ploughs up the steppe of northern Kazakhstan for grain.

events.label: Tashkent earthquake
events.desc: Much of the old city is destroyed on 26 April.

events.label: Uzbekistan declares independence
events.desc: Independence is declared on 31 August.

events.label: Kyrgyzstan declares independence
events.desc: Independence is declared on 31 August.

events.label: Tajikistan declares independence
events.desc: Independence is declared on 9 September.

events.label: Turkmenistan declares independence
events.desc: Independence is declared on 27 October.

events.label: Kazakhstan declares independence
events.desc: The last Soviet republic to do so, on 16 December.

events.label: Kazakhstan moves its capital to Akmola
events.desc: The capital moves north from Almaty; the city is later renamed Astana.

events.label: Kyrgyz Revolution of 2010
events.desc: President Bakiyev is overthrown in April; ethnic violence follows in the south in June.
events.check: no Wikidata item for the linked article

events.label: Death of Islam Karimov
events.desc: Uzbekistan's ruler since before independence dies.

events.label: Kazakh unrest
events.desc: Protests over fuel prices in January turn into the worst violence since independence.
